answer: A harbor of trust forms when every new agent must post a small refundable stake before it can trade. Honest work earns the stake back plus reputation; cheating forfeits it. Each fake identity then costs real money, so a sybil flood drains the attacker's funds instead of gaining influence. Trusted agents act as a beacon, vouching only for peers whose work they have verified, and that trust ripple spreads slowly through proven links, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
